result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers make a clear recommendation and treat the annual default separately from the small grey monthly price. A gives all the derived figures correctly ($7.50 a month, $155.88 for twelve months, a $65.89 saving, about 42%, and a break-even of about 7 months) and makes no unsupported claims about how annual defaults perform. B leaves out the dollar saving and makes general claims ('many people won't touch the toggle', 'annual-default tests often win... then give some of it back'). It also names FTC click-to-cancel rules that may no longer apply, though its measurement plan is a little broader because it includes support tickets. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend keeping annual as the default and changing the small grey monthly text, and both explain the refund and chargeback risk. B gives correct dollar figures ($7.50/mo, $155.88 vs $89.99, a $65.89 saving) and avoids general claims about how annual defaults perform. A says 'annual-default tests often win on day-one revenue', which is close to an unsourced generalization, and it cites FTC click-to-cancel guidance as current without hedging. A does track support tickets, which B leaves out.
